records.summary: User feedback enables LLMs to refine reusable personalized skills, but often mixes persistent preferences with request-specific corrections. Indiscriminately retaining both risks negative transfer, motivating selective retention at the level of individual requirements. We frame this challenge as selective transfer over atomic rules and propose SkillGrain, a framework for learning reusable personalized skills from user feedback. SkillGrain decomposes feedback into independently actionable rules, predicts their transferability, and retains only those suitable for future requests. To learn these decisions, we combine rubric-guided skill rewards with fine-grained credit assignment that …

records.title: T2J-BENCH: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Execution-Grounded PyTorch-to-JAX Repository Migration
records.summary: Migrating a machine-learning codebase across frameworks--for example from PyTorch to JAX--is a routine but costly engineering task that is fundamentally cross-paradigm: eager, stateful, object-oriented modules must be rewritten as pure, jittable functions over an explicit parameter pytree. We ask whether coding agents can perform such whole-repository migrations correctly, and argue that existing code benchmarks, which grade unit-test pass rates or surface-level similarity to a reference translation, cannot answer this: they neither require the migrated system to \emph{behave} the same nor prevent a JAX reimplementation from faking equivalence by secretly importing PyTorch itself. We …

records.title: Evaluating Compressed Memory: Dependence, Utility, and Content Benefit
records.summary: Does a language model answer better because its compressed memory contains useful document information? Replacing memory vectors with zeros can lower a trained model's score without showing that it outperforms a model trained without memory. We combine zeroing with separately trained models that cannot access stored text or receive the same constant input for every document. Across nine systems, some models rely on memory yet perform worse than the trained alternative. For example, in experiments that predict states in generated stories, zeroing memory worsens a model's prediction loss, yet a model trained without memory achieves lower loss than the original model with intact memory. On …

records.title: Beyond Corrected Actions: Training LLM Agents on Textual Critiques
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for multi-turn agentic tasks that require interactions with users and environments over extended sequences of actions. A common approach to improving LLM agents is to use more capable expert models to provide training supervision, either by behavior cloning the expert's trajectories or by using the expert to correct the actions in trajectories generated by the weaker student model. However, expert LLMs can provide richer supervision than actions alone: they can directly generate textual critique that explain why specific actions are incorrect. We study whether training on such feedback benefits LLM agents and propose Critique-Augmented …

records.title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
records.summary: Multimodal models and agents have emerged to enable AI systems to learn from and interact with the real world more like humans by integrating information across multiple modalities. However, enabling multimodal agents to continually acquire useful information from complex, heterogeneous multimodal data remains a significant challenge as they move toward long-horizon tasks and lifelong settings. Addressing this challenge requires effective memory mechanisms that can maintain continuity across sessions, adapt to changing users and environments, and refine memory-management policies through accumulated experience. We introduce a two-axis analytical framework for multimodal agent memory …

records.title: LLMs Can Get "Brain Rot": A Pilot Study on Twitter/X
records.summary: We propose and test the LLM Brain Rot Hypothesis: continual exposure to junk web text induces lasting cognitive decline in large language models (LLMs). To unveil junk effects, we designed a novel controlled experiment on real Twitter/X corpora, by constructing junk and reverse-controlled datasets via two orthogonal operationalizations: M1 (engagement degree) and M2 (semantic quality), with matched token scale and training operations across conditions. Compared to the control group, continual pre-training of 4 LLMs on the junk dataset causes non-trivial declines (Hedges' g>0.3) on reasoning, long-context understanding, safety, and inflating "dark traits" (e.g., psychopathy, narcissism). The …

records.title: Tail Competition Explains Scaling in Best-of-N Sampling for Verifiable Problems
records.summary: Best-of-N sampling is a simple inference-time scaling strategy for large language models, yet its behavior under incomplete reward models remains poorly understood. We study Best-of-N as a competition between the extreme reward tails of correct and incorrect responses. This view shows that success depends not only on the probability of sampling a correct response, but also on whether correct responses dominate incorrect ones in the upper tail. Using extreme value theory, we characterize three asymptotic regimes: correct-tail-dominant, incorrect-tail-dominant, and critical explaining both monotonic gains and reward-hacking-induced degradation. We further derive finite-sample scaling laws for …

records.title: AdaptFuse: Training-Free Sequential Preference Inference via Externalized Bayesian Computation
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) struggle to accumulate evidence across multiple rounds of user interactions, failing to update their beliefs in a manner consistent with Bayesian inference. Existing solutions require fine-tuning on sensitive user interaction data, limiting their applicability in privacy-conscious settings. We propose \textsc{AdaptFuse}, a training-free framework that externalizes probabilistic computation entirely from the LLM, where a symbolic module maintains a Bayesian posterior over a discrete hypothesis set, while a frozen LLM contributes semantic reasoning via multi-sample Dirichlet aggregation. The two signals are combined through entropy-adaptive fusion, which …

records.title: Steering Vectors for Competing Ethical Frameworks Are Interchangeable: A Competing-Target Test for Activation Steering
records.summary: Activation steering adds a vector to a model's hidden states to control a named behaviour. A gain on that behaviour, however, does not show that the vector controls it directly: it may act through a component shared with neighbouring behaviours, which unsteered and random baselines cannot separate. We introduce the competing-target test: a vector is compared with the vector built the same way for a competing target, and an equivalence test states when their difference is below a useful margin. We apply it in open-weight models to vectors for Kantian deontology, which judges an act by the rule it follows, and act utilitarianism, which judges it by the welfare it produces. On held-out …

records.title: SecJev: Bringing Security Expertise to System One Decision Models
records.summary: Security workflows need models that turn complex observations and explicit policies into decisions. System One models introduced by Jev return typed predictions and probabilities; security specialization supplies the domain expertise behind those predictions. We introduce SecJev, to our knowledge the first family of Jev-style decision models specialized for security, spanning 0.8B to 9B parameters. Built on Kev's single-pass candidate scorer, SecJev learns Boolean, choice, and ordered decisions from text, telemetry, and observation histories. We develop SecJev-Corpus to unify source-label prediction and explicit-policy evaluation across 14 tasks and eight sources. It covers tool outputs, …

records.title: When More Documents Hurt RAG: Measuring and Reducing Vector Search Dilution with Domain-Scoped Retrieval
records.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) degrades when applied to large, heterogeneous document collections. In RAG systems, dense similarity becomes less discriminative, causing top-$k$ retrieval to return semantically similar but contextually incorrect chunks. We refer to this failure mode as vector search dilution. Even under hybrid dense+sparse retrieval, we first observed it in a deployed Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT) system; in a controlled experiment, growing the corpus from 54 to 1,128 documents cut precision@10 by 63% and recall of the answer-bearing document by 23%. Similar patterns were observed in six other DOTs. To diagnose this issue, we introduce MASDR-RAG …

records.title: Where to Start, How to Move: Analyzing Curricula under GRPO for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
records.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) provides no reward-relative learning signal when all rollouts receive identical rewards. In long-horizon tasks that require multiple interactions, rewards are given only upon successful task completion, making all-fail groups common early in training and limiting opportunities to practice later steps. Guide Assisted GRPO replays a successful reference prefix before the learner continues. We study how initial positions, handoff units, and movement rules affect unassisted task completion. Across three model sizes on BFCL, starting near completion is more effective under a fixed turn-level threshold rule. Finer handoffs alone do not consistently help, …

records.title: Target-Token Asymmetry Can Masquerade As Depth Specialization
records.summary: Layer-ablation studies often perturb early or late layers of a language model, compare the damage to prediction on two corpora, and read a larger early-layer effect on one corpus as early-layer specialization for its task. Such a comparison averages over the tokens that each corpus asks the model to predict, and these target tokens differ: math solutions, for example, ask for far more whitespace and numbers than encyclopedia prose. We show that this difference can create the appearance of depth specialization. We split a cross-corpus early--late damage interaction by target-token type and recompute it under a target mixture shared by both corpora. Between GSM8K and Wikitext, a positive …

records.title: Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition: Separating Selection from Redistribution in Training-Data Filtering
records.summary: A training-data quality gate changes both which examples survive within regions of the input space and how training mass is distributed across those regions, so a gate-versus-random comparison does not isolate these mechanisms. We introduce Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition (CGSD), a four-arm, budget-matched design that crosses gate eligibility with support distribution and decomposes the observed gate effect into within-support selection, between-support redistribution, and their interaction. The practical constraint is finite-pool realizability: we characterize mass and token-assembly conditions under which the required arms can be constructed, together with a support-extinction …

records.title: LLM-jp-4 Technical Report
records.summary: This paper presents LLM-jp-4, a family of Japanese sovereign large language models (LLMs) developed with an emphasis on transparency, reproducibility, and practical usability. LLM-jp-4 comprises an 8B dense model and a 32B-A3B mixture-of-experts model, both trained from scratch on approximately 12 trillion tokens. To support independent verification and reproduction, we establish explicit criteria for selecting training data, external models, and software, and make the development process publicly available. Evaluation results demonstrate substantial improvements over previous LLM-jp models and competitive performance against open-weight models of similar scale. By documenting the …

records.title: TopicMerge: A Divide and Conquer Approach to Topic Modeling
records.summary: Recent advancements in topic modeling have split into two main paths: efficient embedding-based methods that offer scalability but are often outperformed on standard clustering metrics, and Large Language Model (LLM) approaches that achieve state-of-the-art clustering performance but at the cost of prohibitive computational expense and poor scalability. This paper introduces TopicMerge, a novel multi-stage pipeline that bridges these approaches to achieve both state-of-the-art clustering performance and computational efficiency. TopicMerge first employs an efficient clustering pipeline to deliberately over-segment a document corpus into a large set of fine-grained, semantically pure …

records.title: Truthful and Expected-Payment-Optimal Model Routing in Graph-Based Agentic Workflows
records.summary: Assigning routine tasks to cheaper large language model (LLM) providers can reduce generation cost, but switching providers may require processing accumulated context again. Keeping dependent tasks with the same provider can instead reuse eligible context. Graph-based workflows therefore couple routing decisions across tasks. Independent providers may also privately know their real-time unit costs and strategically misreport them. We formulate this routing problem as a single-parameter procurement auction and propose STAR (Strategy-proof Topology-aware Agent Routing), which minimizes virtual-cost-weighted graph workloads. Its allocation rule and payments, computed by integrating workload …

records.title: PersEvalBench: Can LLM Evaluators Judge Contextually Appropriate Use of Persona Information?
records.summary: Large language model (LLM) evaluators are increasingly used to assess personalized assistants, yet whether they can reliably judge personalization has rarely been tested. We introduce PersEvalBench, a benchmark testing whether an evaluator can recognize appropriate and inappropriate uses of user history. It contains 403 multi-episode scenarios where user information should persist, transfer, or cease to apply. The benchmark covers nine controlled error subtypes across three families: under-personalization, over-personalization, and misapplied-state errors. Human audits confirm that generated errors match their intended types and that the prescribed uses of user information are reasonable. …

records.title: Assessing and Refining ChatGPT's Performance in Identifying Targeting and Inappropriate Language: A Comparative Study
records.summary: This study evaluates the effectiveness of ChatGPT, an advanced AI model for natural language processing, in identifying targeting and inappropriate language in online comments. With the increasing challenge of moderating vast volumes of user-generated content on social network sites, the role of AI in content moderation has gained prominence. We compared ChatGPT's performance against crowd-sourced annotations and expert evaluations to assess its accuracy, scope of detection, and consistency. Our findings show that ChatGPT performs well in detecting inappropriate content, and that almost the entire gain from iterative prompt refinement came from a single change --- simplifying the label …

records.title: Qwenfant: Train Big Character-level BabyLMs on Concise Parallel Text
records.summary: This work concerns our submission for the Multilingual track of the 2026 BabyLM Challenge. We improve on our baseline using data that has been summarized and translated by an LLM, showing that higher-quality data can come from synthetic sources. We further improve with 2 simple changes: using a larger model, and using a character-level vocabulary. Both of these changes require LoRA-style fine-tuning for realizing their full potential. We dub our final Qwen3-based model Qwenfant, which, at the time of submission, ranks 1st in the Multilingual track.

records.title: Can LLM Agents Efficiently Identify Appliance Faults? Insights From Diagnosing a Simulated Appliance
records.summary: In so-called "Industry 4.0," integrated sensors, analytics tools, and other digital technologies supplement industrial workflows, potentiating enhanced visibility and automation. Prognostics and health management (PHM) and natural language processing (NLP) practitioners alike have explored the application of large language models (LLMs) to industrial asset management, but many prior works' focus on exam-like benchmarks has limited their assessment of LLMs' ability to automate practical operations. Herein, we introduce CoffeeBench, a fault diagnostics task for LLM agents, using a simulated appliance. The LLMs we evaluate struggle to consistently identify faults from the sensor information …

records.title: From Efficiency to Sufficiency: The Cost-Aware Measurement Design Framework for Automated Essay Scoring
records.summary: Compute cost in automated essay scoring (AES) is usually treated as a technical efficiency issue rather than a measurement design concern. Yet deployment decisions require more than reporting latency, model size, or inference expense. In high-stakes settings, total burden includes validation, monitoring, adjudication, compliance, and governance; in instructional settings, pricing, licensing, and integration may dominate cost. This paper reframes AES as a cost-constrained measurement system and introduces the Cost-Aware Measurement Design (CAMD) Framework, a four-layer structure consisting of metering, allocation, unit economics, and decision, for translating computational and workflow …

records.title: EduBehaviors: Assertion-based Schemas for Auditable Coding of Educational Dialogues
records.summary: Large language models have enabled rapid deployment of language classification and analysis, allowing users to describe complex constructs in natural language, such as pedagogical moves or expressions of learning and engagement, and label them in conversational datasets such as classroom or tutoring transcripts. However, because LLM reasoning is opaque, we have no verifiable, mechanistic insight into why a model chose a label for an utterance, and output differences over time or across models challenge replication. We introduce the EduBehaviors framework to generate interpretable, reliable, and scalable construct annotations in educational dialogue data that retain human agency while …

records.title: Whose Data, Whose Benchmark? A User-Centric Framework for Auditing Evaluation Resources
records.summary: Benchmarks shape how model capabilities are measured and interpreted, yet their scores can obscure whose conventions, contexts, and judgments define successful performance. We introduce a user-centric audit framework that distinguishes users who contribute benchmark content from those whose needs evaluation results are intended to represent. The framework operationalizes seven dimensions across benchmark content, metadata, documentation, and scoring procedures. Across 16 resources, we find that American-centered conventions account for 62.4-94.4% of matched signals in 11 text benchmarks, while geographic visibility in five image-text resources is concentrated and strongly associated with …

records.title: MemeTrace: A Multimodal LLM-Based Agent for Safety-Aware Meme Provenance Analysis
records.summary: Online memes are often carriers of unsafe content such as disinformation and propaganda. Their rapid evolution in response to news events and strong dependence on contextual information make it difficult for platforms and moderators to detect and moderate them effectively. Moreover, existing moderation studies typically classify memes as safe or unsafe based on individual images, lacking the ability to perform broader provenance analysis, i.e., where a meme originates, how it spreads, what cultural symbolism it represents, whether it poses potential risks to society, etc. To bridge this gap, we introduce MemeTrace, a multimodal LLM-based agent that automatically traces the provenance and …

records.title: Policy-Conditioned AI-Use Detection: An Evidentiary Framework for Academic Publishing
records.summary: Major venues now publish detailed rules about how authors, reviewers, and area chairs may use AI, and those rules differ by role, by task, and by what must be disclosed. AI detection, the instrument usually proposed to enforce them, estimates something else: whether an AI model wrote the text. We argue that this target is misaligned with the decisions conferences and journals face, and propose policy-conditioned AI-use detection, an evidentiary framework for assessing whether a human--AI workflow complied with a stated rule. records.title: When Is Enough Not Enough? Illusory Completion in Search Agents
records.summary: In agentic search, an LLM agent searches the web, reads the pages it finds, and decides what to look for next before returning an answer. But can we trust an answer simply because the agent returns it? Often not, and even a correct answer can be a lucky guess: on questions with several constraints, we find that agents conclude the task is complete while a constraint remains unverified in up to 48% of their correct answers. We call this illusory completion. To see how it arises, we introduce the Epistemic Ledger, which tracks at every turn what the retrieved pages establish about each constraint and what the agent claims. records.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
records.summary: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. records.title: Majority Bit-Aware Watermarking For Large Language Models
records.summary: The growing deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) has raised concerns about their misuse in generating harmful or deceptive content. To address this issue, watermarking methods have been proposed to embed identifiable multi-bit messages into generated text for misuse tracing. However, existing methods often suffer from a fundamental trade-off between text quality and decoding accuracy. In particular, they have to restrict the size of the preferred token set (i.e., green list) during encoding to maintain a detectable watermark signal for decoding, which inevitably degrades generation quality. To improve this trade-off, we propose a novel message encoding paradigm called \textit{majority …

records.title: Do Syntax Heads Influence Model Behavior?
records.summary: Transformer language models develop attention heads that specialize in syntactic relations, for example, attending from verbs to their subjects. Do these heads play a causal role in the model's syntactic predictions? Evidence for such a role is mixed to negative: even when we force these heads to attend to a distractor noun other than the subject, the model's syntactic predictions are still more consistent with the subject than with the distractor. Interventions on specialized syntax heads had a significantly stronger effect on syntactic predictions than interventions on random heads, but only in one of the two measures we propose.

records.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
records.summary: Agentic video creation systems remain far from cinematic-grade quality: their underlying models struggle to plan how story, characters, visuals, and sound fit together, and high-quality creation trajectories to learn such planning abilities are scarce. Finished human films embody this knowledge, but in a tightly coupled audiovisual form that agents cannot directly read or manipulate. We propose the Agentic Video Auto-Encoder (AVA-Encoder), which works backward from finished films, turning them into agent-native representations with reconstruction itself as supervision. records.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
records.summary: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. records.title: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning for Automated Reward Design
records.summary: Crafting effective reward signals remains a central challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) for complex reasoning. Existing methods for automated reward optimization search with a fixed proposer which never learns from its costly trials. We present Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (DERL), a dual-training framework for autonomous discovery of reward structures. An outer-loop proposer composes a reward from task primitives, and an inner policy trains with this reward. The proposer itself learns by policy gradient from the validation performance of the inner policy. records.title: PLACID: Privacy-preserving Large language models for Acronym Clinical Inference and Disambiguation
records.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer transformative solutions across many domains, but healthcare integration is hindered by strict data privacy constraints. Clinical narratives are dense with ambiguous acronyms, misinterpretation these abbreviations can precipitate severe outcomes like life-threatening medication errors. While cloud-dependent LLMs excel at Acronym Disambiguation, transmitting Protected Health Information to external servers violates privacy frameworks. To bridge this gap, this study pioneers the evaluation of small-parameter models deployed entirely on-device to ensure privacy preservation. records.title: Weighted Ensemble Sampling for Rare-Event Estimation in Language Models
records.summary: Rare but severe failures of large language models can become practically significant at deployment scale. Estimating their probabilities with direct Monte Carlo sampling is highly inefficient, while proposal-based methods typically require auxiliary learning of an additional proposal distribution. We introduce \textbf{Weighted Ensemble (WE)}, a training-free framework for rare-event estimation in language models. WE samples exclusively from the original language model and improves upon direct Monte Carlo by periodically reallocating the sampling budget toward prefixes that appear more likely to reach the target rare event. records.title: Is This Just Fantasy? Language Model Representations Reflect Human Judgments of Event Plausibility
records.summary: Language models (LMs) are used for a diverse range of tasks, from question answering to writing fantastical stories. In order to reliably accomplish these tasks, LMs must be able to discern the modal category of a sentence (i.e., whether it describes something that is possible, impossible, completely nonsensical, etc.). However, recent studies have called into question the ability of LMs to categorize sentences according to modality (Michaelov et al., 2025; Kauf et al., 2023). In this work, we identify linear representations that discriminate between modal categories within a variety of LMs, or modal difference vectors. Analysis of modal difference vectors reveals that LMs have access to …

records.title: Confidently Wrong: Detecting Hallucinations in Financial Question Answering from LLM Internal States
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) in financial applications fail most consequentially when they are confidently wrong. Hedged, uncertain answers invite scrutiny, whereas confident errors silently degrade downstream decisions without warning. We ask how reliably such confidently wrong answers, or confident hallucinations, can be detected from a model's internal activations, and whether those activations carry information beyond its output-level confidence signals. We train linear probes on the residual stream and evaluate them on two established numerical question-answering (QA) benchmarks built from real filings, FinQA and TAT-QA. records.title: NEPSEE: A Double-Annotated Benchmark for Nepali Sentiment Analysis
records.summary: Many sentiment datasets use one annotator for each item, so the test labels show the conventions of that person. We build a Nepali benchmark from two annotators who labelled the same sentences blind. They labelled 5,614 sentences from tweets of Nepali public figures on a five-point scale. We keep only the 3,189 sentences where both give the same polarity. On the three-class benchmark, NepBERTa with a fixed tokenizer gets a macro-F1 of 0.877 and IndicBERTv2 0.867. records.title: How to Evaluate When You Don't Know How to Evaluate? Choosing Reliable Setups for Base Language Model Benchmarking
records.summary: Evaluation of large language models (LLMs) remains largely pre-scientific: it involves many design decisions, with little guidance on how to make them. These choices can substantially affect measured performance and, consequently, decisions about subsequent pretraining. To identify effective evaluation setups, we investigate 8 aspects, such as task formulation or the number of in-context examples. We compare the setups using three widely-used signal criteria, repurposed as normative meta-measures: monotonicity, non-randomness, and ranking consistency of the evaluation scores across intermediate checkpoints. records.title: Document-as-Image Representations Fall Short for Scientific Retrieval
records.summary: Many recent document embedding models are trained on document-as-image representations, embedding rendered pages as images rather than the underlying source. Meanwhile, existing benchmarks for scientific document retrieval, such as ArXivQA and ViDoRe, treat documents as images of pages, implicitly favoring such representations. In this work, we argue that this paradigm is not well-suited for text-rich multimodal scientific documents, where critical evidence is distributed across structured sources, including text, tables, and figures. To study this setting, we introduce ArXivDoc, a new benchmark constructed from the underlying LaTeX sources of scientific papers. Unlike PDF or image-based …

records.title: Fantastic Metrics and How to Find Them: Meta-Evaluating Metrics for Multi-lingual Style-Personalized Generation
records.summary: Meta-evaluation of text generation metrics and LLM-judges is primarily conducted using metric-human correlations. However, prior work has shown that correlation is not an appropriate estimate of a metric's evaluation capability and can be unstable across evaluation settings, such as different datasets or languages. Therefore, we propose a regression-based meta-evaluation of metrics that learns on calibrated metric outputs to predict human ratings. We ground this measurement relative to a trivial constant-mean baseline and human agreements to provide a comparable measure of metric capability across evaluation settings. To test our meta-evaluation framework, we developed a large-scale …

records.title: ListQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating List-Formatted Factual Knowledge Retrieval in Large Language Models
records.summary: Many real-world questions demand not a single fact but an organized collection of them, yet existing factual knowledge benchmarks almost exclusively target single answer retrieval. We introduce ListQA, a benchmark of 9,045 human-curated, cross-validated questions (audited error rate of 1.7%) that require LLMs to recall multiple facts and compose them into structured lists of 3-10 elements. Questions range from flat lists ("Which NCAA teams went undefeated between 2000 and 2024?") to hierarchical lists with sub-attributes ("...and what was their record and result?"), spanning eight categories across 60+ countries. An evergreen design (explicit temporal constraints or historically immutable …

records.title: From Qualitative Text to Integrated Evidence: The Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI) Procedure
records.summary: Mixed methods research offers established strategies for integrating qualitative and quantitative evidence, but less guidance for integrating two computational representations of the same qualitative corpus. This methodological study introduces Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI), a four-step procedure for explicit and traceable integration. We present PTI using 1,203 interview paragraphs from 29 mothers in Nepal. The two representations were ontology-guided Patient Voice (PV) coding with PVminer and data-driven themes generated through non-negative matrix factorization (NMF). records.title: CALM-IT: Enhancing Synthetic Motivational Interviewing Dialogue Quality with Conversational Dynamics
records.summary: Conversational dynamics describe how rapport, emotion, and goals change over a dialogue. These changes are important in therapeutic conversations, where they can influence when and how therapists intervene. However, large language model (LLM)-based synthetic therapeutic dialogue generators rarely track how these properties evolve together, which may limit the quality of longer conversations. We introduce CALM-IT, a dual-agent framework that tracks client states and therapist-side inferences to guide strategy selection and utterance generation. records.title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
records.summary: Can AI agents carry out research on open scientific problems? We introduce Into the Unknown, a benchmark that provides an agent with a science paper along with a research direction to pursue and tasks it to write a follow-up paper. We work with scientists at US Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, who each contribute an unpublished follow-up direction from their own work together with the necessary conditions a submission must meet. While assessing the quality of a follow-up paper is challenging in general, using these conditions to form a rubric makes evaluation more tractable for research problems that have no reference answer. records.title: DivAlgo: A systematic evaluation of algorithmic diversity for code generation models
records.summary: Code generation models are actively being used in professional and educational settings. However, the competence of large language models (LLMs) to generate algorithmically diverse code remains largely unknown. We propose the DivAlgo benchmark, a large-scale dataset constituting algorithmically diverse solutions to programming problems. We also introduce a lightweight similarity metric to enable large-scale evaluation. records.title: When Can Digital Personas Reliably Approximate Human Survey Findings?
records.summary: Digital personas powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as substitutes for human survey respondents, yet it remains unclear when they can reliably approximate human survey findings. We answer this question using the LISS panel, constructing personas from respondents' background variables and pre-2023 survey histories, then testing them against the same respondents' held-out post-cutoff answers. Across four persona architectures, three LLMs, and two prediction tasks, we assess performance at the question, respondent, distributional, equity, and clustering levels. Digital personas improve alignment with human response distributions, especially in domains tied to …

records.title: MA-Bench: Measuring Operational Planning in Language Models
records.summary: How well can a language model turn a large, incomplete and partly contradictory body of documents into a plan when no single correct answer exists? We introduce Mission Analysis (MA)-Bench, built on mission analysis, the first step of military operational planning, in which a staff reads the full situation and states the problem before anyone proposes a solution. Its 10 expert-built scenarios pair synthetic packets of ten to twelve documents with 1,257 expert-written pass/fail requirements, each containing information on their source, question type, and importance level. records.title: CAFE: Confining Feature Distillation to Language-Routed Adapters for Compact Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
records.summary: Feature distillation is usually expected to add to logit distillation. records.summary: Maintenance work orders are the largest written record of how industrial equipment fails, yet in most plants they are close to unusable for analysis. records.summary: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. records.title: DecisionRobust: Benchmarking Robustness for JEV Style Decision Models Across Text and Vision
records.summary: Emerging decision models such as JEV provide typed interfaces that map task instructions and observations directly to choices, judgments, and scores. records.title: From Copying to Composition: How Language Models Develop In-Context Learning
records.summary: In-context learning (ICL) allows language models to adapt their behavior from instructions and demonstrations in a prompt, but accuracy alone does not reveal how contextual information controls their predictions. records.title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
records.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. records.title: RATIO: A Benchmark for Retrieval Across Typed Ideation Operations in Scientific Literature
records.summary: Retrieved scientific literature can serve as inspiration for both human and AI scientists. records.title: Lazy Grounding: Attacking Search Agents with Factual Evidence
records.summary: Search agents mitigate hallucination by grounding their answers in retrieved web results. records.title: Beyond Aggregate Accuracy: Item-Level Transitions in Prompt Optimization
records.summary: Automatic prompt optimization (APO) uses feedback from model responses to improve prompts automatically. records.title: SWE-Spot: Building Small Repo-Experts with Repository-Centric Learning
records.summary: The deployment of coding agents in privacy-sensitive and resource-constrained environments drives the demand for capable open-weight Small Language Models (SLMs). However, they suffer from a fundamental capability gap: unlike frontier large models, they lack the inference-time strong generalization to handle complicated, unfamiliar codebases. records.title: Smart Alone, Blind Together: Why Accuracy Fails to CertifyTheory of Mind in Multi-Agent Teams
records.summary: Coordinators that act on what they infer about teammates are usually certified by the accuracy of those inferences. We argue that accuracy is the wrong certificate, for two reasons. records.title: Pre-Trained Language Models as Zero-Shot Tools for Social Science Research
records.summary: Record linkage and demographic inference from names are routine demands in social science. records.summary: Pluralistic alignment needs to accommodate diverse preferences under limited human feedback. records.summary: Modern ML research increasingly faces an evaluation bottleneck: building benchmarks and running experiments is costly, slowing iteration. Existing methods often rely on external scorers or heuristic signals only indirectly tied to the model's internal answer computation. We instead adopt a model-internal perspective: as the model forms an answer, each reasoning token induces a ripple in the residual stream whose effect on the answer reflects the token's contribution to the underlying computation. Building on this view, we propose \textsc{MIST} …

records.title: Semantics as a Shield: Label Disguise Defense (LDD) against Prompt Injection in LLM Sentiment Classification
records.summary: Prompt injection can cause large language models (LLMs) to deviate from their intended tasks by following instructions embedded in untrusted input. We investigate whether changing a classifier's output labels improves accuracy under such attacks, using sentiment classification as a case study. Label Disguise Defense (LDD) replaces positive/negative with alternatives such as good/bad or cat/dog, introduced through demonstrations, and maps predictions back to sentiment classes. We analyze retained aggregate results for 200 IMDb reviews, nine recorded model configurations, and eight alternative label pairs under a fixed attack that always requests the incorrect class using the original labels. …

records.title: DeltaTTG: Training Multi-Turn Agents with a Token-to-Go Progress Meter
records.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for multi-turn agents relies on sparse terminal rewards that say little about individual steps. Within-group step comparisons depend on reliable state matching and sufficiently diverse sampled outcomes, while direct step scoring may require costly external evaluators, human annotations, or task-specific heuristics. We introduce DeltaTTG to learn a reusable progress signal through a shared progress meter, using low-cost supervision from diverse policies' recorded trajectories without task-specific progress rules. Its supervision target, Token-to-Go (TTG), the number of tokens remaining to be generated until task completion, serves as an …

records.title: The Image Still Has a Say: Final-Answer Repair for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought
records.summary: Although chain-of-thought prompting has improved multimodal reasoning, it is still difficult to produce correct final answers, as the reasoning can drift away from the image. Besides, the trace is already fixed when the answer is generated, leaving no room for self-correction. Considering the image is still available at the final-answer step, we think it is reasonable to fix the answer there without rewriting the reasoning. As such, the problem becomes to correct the final answer using the image under fixed reasoning. Unlike methods that improve trace generation through training, resampling, or decoding-time grounding, we repair the final-answer readout while keeping the reasoning trace …

records.title: STAGE: Source-grounded Text-to-JSON Artifact GEneration
records.summary: From financial filings to clinical records, legacy industries rely heavily on long, unstructured documents to store high-value information. Reliably extracting this information into structured, machine-readable representations is a key prerequisite to making the contents accessible to automated systems. JSON is a natural target for such structured extraction, yet constructing reliable and scalable text-to-JSON training data remains challenging. To address this gap, we propose STAGE (Spreadsheet-grounded Text-to-JSON Artifact GEneration), a source-grounded data generation pipeline that constructs reports and JSON schema by using LLMs for scalable synthesis while validating ground-truth …

records.title: Worth Their Weights? Evaluating Generative Models for Discourse Parsing
records.summary: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) parsing has historically been dominated by discriminative models based on pretrained encoder-only language models. The recent availability of high-quality generative language models has made it unclear whether RST parsing is better approached as a generative task. In this work, we investigate whether generative language models are better at parsing RST than traditional discriminative ones. We find that at matched parameter counts, discriminative parsers perform much better than generative ones, though much larger generative models sometimes outperform them. Generative models hold a particular advantage in elementary discourse unit (EDU) segmentation, and we …

records.title: Decouple to Forget: Semantic Mediation for Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
records.summary: Machine unlearning for large language models seeks to remove specified knowledge while preserving general capability, yet current methods often treat an entire response as the unit of forgetting. This coarse granularity causes unnecessary utility loss when the forget target is only a small set of sensitive facts embedded within otherwise benign explanations. In this paper, we introduce Decouple to Forget (D2F), a targeted unlearning method inspired by semantic mediation that separates sensitive factual content from non-sensitive meaning and surface expression. For each example to be forgotten, D2F extracts a fact-level "mediator" representation from the answer, identifies which parts are …

records.title: Scaling Creative Writing Beyond Story-Centric Data with Attribute-Guided Genre Expansion
records.summary: High-quality creative writing data for large language models (LLMs) remains dominated by story-centric data, limiting models' ability to follow the structural and functional conventions of diverse creative formats. We propose an attribute-guided genre expansion framework for scaling creative writing data beyond story generation. By separating thematic breadth from genre-form control, our framework leverages human-authored story prompts as diverse creative seeds, while utilizing manually curated genre attributes to enforce distinct structural, stylistic, and formatting conventions. We combine these to prompt strong LLMs for genre-faithful query-response pairs, which are then …

records.title: From Individuals to Interactions: Benchmarking Gender Bias in Multimodal Large Language Models from the Lens of Social Relationship
records.summary: Ensuring the trustworthiness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) requires rigorous evaluation of gender bias, particularly in socially sensitive domains. Existing benchmarks primarily assess bias in isolated contexts and are less suited to capturing biases that emerge through interpersonal interactions. We introduce Genres, a benchmark for evaluating gender bias in MLLMs through the lens of social relationships in narrative generation. Grounded in Fiske's relational models theory, Genres comprises 1,440 multimodal narrative elicitation pairs spanning four fundamental relationship types, diverse social scenarios, and three age groups. Its dual-character generation tasks elicit …

records.title: DisaggKD: Efficient Knowledge Distillation through Teacher-Student Disaggregation and a Fused Loss
records.summary: Knowledge distillation (KD) frameworks place teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits the teachers that fit. DisaggKD separates them across nodes: teacher replicas stream hidden states to the student, a KD loss over row windows and vocabulary shards equals the full-vocabulary loss in exact arithmetic without forming the full-vocabulary logits, and a prefetch ring paces producer and trainer. Closed-form memory and traffic models locate the memory limits of each layout. On the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 9B pair, the disaggregated layout matches the LM loss of the colocated run with the same loss and is faster than that run; our fused loss also lets a colocated run train on as …

records.title: GUARD: Guided Unlearning and Retention via Data Attribution for Large Language Models
records.summary: Unlearning large language models (LLMs) is important due to copyright and privacy concerns. A key challenge is unintended forgetting, where removing data inadvertently impairs model utility. While prior work has focused on architectural innovations, the influence of data-level factors remains underexplored. We introduce GUARD, a framework for **G**uided **U**nlearning **A**nd **R**etention via **D**ata Attribution. GUARD uses a lightweight proxy data attribution metric tailored to LLM unlearning, which efficiently quantifies the "alignment" between the Forget and Retain (or synthetic supplement) Sets. This metric leads to a new unlearning objective that assigns adaptive, nonuniform weights …

records.title: TopoCurate:Modeling Interaction Topology for Tool-Use Agent Training
records.summary: Training tool-use agents typically relies on outcome-based filtering: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on successful trajectories and Reinforcement Learning (RL) on pass-rate-selected tasks. However, this paradigm ignores interaction dynamics: successful trajectories may lack error recovery or exhibit redundancy, while pass rates fail to distinguish structurally informative tasks from trivial ones. We propose \textbf{TopoCurate}, an interaction-aware framework that projects multi-trial rollouts from the same task into a unified semantic quotient topology. records.title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures
records.summary: Work on debugging LLM agents treats the "first mistake" marked by a human or LLM judge as ground truth for where a trajectory failed. We ask whether such labels point at causes or symptoms, and make the distinction executable: we restart the agent from reconstructed intermediate states of a failed trajectory and estimate its prefix value V(h_t), the probability of success from each step, with a certified point of no return (PNR) for a failure. On 150 SWE-bench Verified tasks with two frozen open-weight agents, we build such curves for 47 and 60 failed trajectories and probe every step labeled by four frontier judges under the Traverse rubric. records.title: Gödel Forest: Balancing Search Depth and Breadth for Data-Centric Recursive Self-Improvement
records.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) aims to achieve compounding gains by having models improve themselves. While most existing RSI systems optimize external agent harnesses or prompts around a frozen base model, data-centric RSI directly updates the model's own parameters by training on agent-generated data. However, because validating data strategies requires expensive model training, existing methods face a fundamental dilemma: a single agent gets trapped in narrow directions and lacks exploration breadth, while naive parallel search or heavy trace sharing sacrifices long-horizon search depth. To address this challenge, we introduce G"odel Forest, a multi-agent framework that organizes …

records.title: When Does an ASR Error Matter? Task-Role Diagnostics for Tool-Using Voice Agents
records.summary: In cascaded voice agents, ASR errors can have markedly different downstream consequences: a small transcription error may leave a tool call unchanged or alter its intent or arguments. Conventional word error rate (WER), however, does not capture these differences. We introduce SpeechEvalX, a paired diagnostic protocol that evaluates how task roles affected by ASR errors influence structured tool calls. Controlled edits are matched by source utterance, edit count, and operation, while task-role labels are compared with lexical severity, BERT cosine distance, Semantic-WER, and binary criticality. records.title: StateHarness: Maintaining Evolving Project State for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
records.summary: Long-horizon coding requires agents to maintain an evolving view of the project they are changing: what problem is currently being solved, what has already been learned or modified, which other artifacts may be affected, and what work remains unresolved. When this information is scattered across a growing interaction history, local edits can become disconnected from their later consequences and progress can be difficult to carry forward. We introduce StateHarness, a runtime framework that maintains evolving project state without updating model parameters. The working agent records its current problem and hypothesis, important findings and decisions, discovered repository relationships, and …

records.title: DREAM: Dynamic Resolution Assignment For Multimodal Multi-agent Debate
records.summary: Multi-agent debate (MAD) has emerged as an effective paradigm to improve the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and is increasingly being extended to multimodal settings. However, existing multimodal MAD frameworks typically expose agents to the same fixed visual input, ignoring substantial variation in the visual scale needed across samples and agents. In addition, these frameworks frequently suffer from groupthink, a phenomenon where agents prematurely abandon correct deductions to conform with confident but hallucinated peer responses. To address these bottlenecks, we introduce DREAM (Dynamic Resolution Assignment For Multimodal Multi-Agent Debate), which operates via …

records.title: Facts Don't Speak Louder than Words: The Behavioral Essence of Long-CoT Distillation
records.summary: While long chain-of-thought (CoT) distillation significantly improves the reasoning abilities of language models, its underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. Current pipelines generally rely on rejection sampling to gather reasoning traces across diverse prompts, assuming that factual correctness and broad problem coverage are indispensable. Surprisingly, we find that training exclusively on flawed reasoning trajectories or a restricted prompt set yields nearly comparable performance. records.title: Multidimensional Consistency Improves Reasoning in Language Models
records.summary: While Large language models (LLMs) have proved able to address some complex reasoning tasks, we also know that they are highly sensitive to input variation, which can lead to different solution paths and final answers. Answer consistency across input variations can thus be taken as a sign of stronger confidence. Leveraging this aspect, we introduce a framework where models are \textit{systematically pushed to diversify solution paths} towards a final answer, thereby testing them for answer consistency across multiple input variations. Focusing on math problems, we induce variations in (i) order of shots in prompt, (ii) problem phrasing, and (iii) languages used. Experiments on a wide range …

records.title: Cross-Lingual Steering for Figurative Language Generation
records.summary: Cross-lingual activation steering has been studied mainly for language-agnostic properties such as factual knowledge and reasoning. Its transferability remains unclear for figurative language, whose expressions are often tied to a particular language. In this work, we study cross-lingual steering of figurative language: whether steering vectors learned in one language can affect generation in another. We first show that within a single language, steering effectively increases the ratio of the intended figure of speech, especially for metaphor and idiom. records.title: TDR: Tagalog Diacritic Restoration Dataset
records.summary: Homographs are words that share identical spelling but differ in meaning and pronunciation. In Tagalog, these distinctions are disambiguated in writing through tuldik (diacritical marks), which are rarely preserved in contemporary Tagalog text. This scarcity of diacritics limits diacritic restoration, which is useful for downstream tasks such as prosody selection for text-to-speech synthesis. To address this gap, this study introduces TDR, an annotated corpus of 40 frequent Tagalog homographs constructed from news text. It also introduces a collocation-driven retrieval method to expand the dataset and mitigate severe class imbalance among minor variants. Finally, we show that TDR supplies a …

records.title: Tanawpamana: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Philippine Cultural Heritage Sites
records.summary: Vision-language models are increasingly used to identify and describe places, yet their recognition and knowledge of specific cultures remain poorly understood, particularly in underrepresented regions such as the Philippines. This study introduces the Tanawpamana Dataset, a repository of Philippine heritage site images with metadata based on the Talapamana registry of the National Commission for Culture and the Arts of the Philippines. We also introduce the Tanawpamana Benchmark, comprising 4,046 tasks designed to evaluate models' recognition and knowledge of heritage sites. Evaluating seven vision-language models, we find that they struggle more with fine-grained visual discrimination …

records.title: KMMMU: Evaluation of Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding in Korean Language and Context
records.summary: Multimodal evaluation is strengthened when benchmarks reflect the languages, institutions, and disciplinary conventions that shape expert visual reasoning. We introduce KMMMU, a native Korean benchmark built from Korean-native examination materials. KMMMU contains 3,466 questions spanning nine disciplines and nine visual modality categories. For targeted evaluation on challenging questions and Korean-specific knowledge, we additionally provide KMMMU-Adv and KMMMU-Local, respectively. Experiments show that the strongest evaluated open-weight model reaches 42.05% on the KMMMU, while the best evaluated proprietary model achieves 52.42% on the KMMMU-Adv. records.title: Self-Improving Language Models with Bidirectional Evolutionary Search
records.summary: Search has been proposed as an effective method for self-improving language models and agentic systems, both for post-training sample generation and for inference. However, widely used methods such as best-of-N sampling and tree search face two fundamental limitations: they are guided by sparse verification signals, and they construct candidates primarily through autoregressive expansion, restricting exploration to regions with substantial model probability mass. To address these, we propose Bidirectional Evolutionary Search (BES), a search framework that couples forward candidate evolution with backward goal decomposition. records.title: Decision Models vs. LLMs as Rubric Judges: Cheaper, Faster, and Wrong in the Same Places
records.summary: LLM judges now score outputs against rubrics, in benchmarks and as training rewards. Decision models return probabilities over permitted answers with a confidence score but no free text. Two such models are Jev and an open reproduction, Perplexity's Decider. We compare each with three flash-tier LLM judges on nine panels from seven benchmarks with human judgments, giving every judge identical criterion texts. The LLM judges run in two setups, reading a whole rubric at once or one criterion at a time. Our findings suggest both decision models can often stand in for them. records.title: Dissociating Answerability from Extraction in LLM Question Answering over Radiology Reports
records.summary: Answering questions from radiology reports involves two decisions: whether the report contains an answer and which span gives it. A false answer presents an unsupported claim as fact; an over-abstention hides what the report says. Yet RadQA results are reported as a single F1 that merges both. We propose an evaluation method that separates them, reporting false-answer and over-abstention rates beside F1 and splitting F1 changes into extraction and answerability terms. We apply it to 13 LLMs on the RadQA test set, zero-shot and with three cumulative demonstration sets, the last adding an unanswerable example. Models with similar F1 differed more than twofold in false-answer rate. The …

records.title: Improving Heart-Focused Medical Question Answering in LLMs via Variance-Aware Rubric Rewards with GRPO
records.summary: Large language models can support medical question answering, but privacy, cost, and reliability still limit their clinical use in focused domains. Can rubric-based reinforcement learning bring a locally deployable model close to much larger systems? We study Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for heart-focused medical question answering with rubric supervision from RaR-Medicine. Rather than rely on binary rubric aggregation or a single overall score, our variance-aware reward framework builds continuous rewards from criterion-level outcomes. records.title: Reference Wording Shapes Retrieval of Robot Task Instructions
records.summary: Identifying a robot task from a short instruction is sensitive to which descriptions are available for retrieval. We investigate this effect in the natural-language instructions included with the RLBench manipulation benchmark. We extract 296 fixed descriptions from 62 publicly available task files and compare five training-free lexical rankers over 80 random choices of one indexed description per task. Exact strings assigned to conflicting task labels are excluded from the primary score. Character n-gram TF-IDF achieves 61.3% mean top-1 accuracy on the resulting held-out instructions, compared with 55.6% for BM25 and 54.9% for word TF-IDF. records.title: MoLE: Mixture of Latent Experts for Complementary Visual Reasoning
records.summary: Latent visual reasoning equips vision--language models with continuous intermediate states that can process visual evidence without explicit textual reasoning traces or repeated image operations. However, existing methods often allow multiple latent tokens to access the same visual evidence through shared value projections, providing no mechanism for them to extract complementary visual information; simply increasing the latent budget can therefore yield redundant latent representations. We argue that effective latent reasoning should encourage different latent tokens to extract complementary visual information, and thereby act as specialized visual experts. records.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents
records.summary: Thought templates, skill libraries, agent memories and caches turn many reasoning steps into one. We call this reasoning contraction. A contracted memory saves reasoning steps and errors until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong. Most systems trust memories by counting successes and failures. We prove that such counters are badly tuned change detectors: a symmetric counter notices a partial change only after a power of its false-alarm horizon, and an unclipped one may never notice it. records.title: Beyond Unsafe Detection: Counterfactually Anchored Evidence Attribution for Multi-Turn LLM Safety Failures
records.summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) move from conversational assistants to advanced agentic systems, guardrail failures can convert adversarial intents into harmful executions. However, most evaluation frameworks focus only on whether a user request is unsafe. This is insufficient for multi-turn failures, where adversarial intent may be distributed across turns and emerge only from accumulated context. This motivates us to go beyond detection to localize the evidence that pushes the conversation toward unsafe trajectories. We introduce MTAG-Bench, a multi-turn guardrail attribution dataset with behavioral validation and counterfactual supervision containing 4,167 conversations. We also …

records.title: Everyone Was Right: Lexical Representations in Language Models Are Both Abstract and Holistic
records.summary: Lexical representations can encode both abstract information and information specific to particular contexts. We investigate how these forms of information are organized in language models by decomposing contextual word representations into item, class, and word-class interaction components. Across six pretrained transformers and two linguistic categories, we find that the interaction is consistently present, grows across layers, and contains information associated with both item and class. Unlike the nearly orthogonal item and class effects, the interaction overlaps with both and encodes class information beyond the shared class effect. records.title: Soohak: A Mathematician-Curated Benchmark for Evaluating Research-level Math Capabilities of LLMs
records.summary: Following the recent achievement of gold-medal performance on the IMO by frontier LLMs, the community is searching for the next meaningful and challenging target for measuring LLM reasoning. Whereas olympiad-style problems measure step-by-step reasoning alone, research-level problems use such reasoning to advance the frontier of mathematical knowledge itself, emerging as a compelling alternative. Yet research-level math benchmarks remain scarce because such problems are difficult to source (e.g., Riemann Bench and FrontierMath-Tier 4 contain 25 and 50 problems, respectively). To support reliable evaluation of next-generation frontier models, we introduce Soohak, a 439-problem benchmark …

records.title: The Holistic Storage of Verb+Up Phrases in Text-based and Audio-based Language Models
records.summary: One of the most central aspects of language processing is the ability to trade off between stored representations and abstract knowledge: one must retrieve stored representations, but also generate novel ones by applying productive rules. While recent work has examined abstract knowledge in language models, holistic storage has received far less attention. We probe internal representations in both text-based LLMs and an ASR model, testing whether V+up phrasal verbs develop distinct representations as a function of frequency and predictability. All models show evidence of holistic storage driven by frequency and predictability, further supporting usage-based theories of language.

records.title: Behavioral History Outperforms Descriptions of the Person for LLM Synthetic Personas
records.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as synthetic personas representing survey respondents. Their validity as substitutes for particular respondents depends on whether they reproduce individuals' decisions. We examine what information helps synthetic respondents predict each individual's later choices, using five conditions that add progressively richer information: no personal information, demographics, personality traits, cognitive scores, and finally the respondent's earlier survey choices as behavioral history. records.title: A Sense of Proprioception in Language Models
records.summary: In humans, proprioception corresponds to the sense of self-movement or position, e.g. understanding the position of one's arm. This sense is often less well-understood and in popular understanding sometimes conflated with introspection. But, notably, proprioception is a separate sense, with dedicated receptors and verifiable outcomes. On the other hand though, language models cannot observe their own internal states during training (and for example answer the question which experts activated in a certain layer of an MoE) and so cannot accurately report on them. records.title: From Associations to Activations: Comparing Behavioral and Hidden-State Semantic Geometry in LLMs
records.summary: We investigate the extent to which an LLM's hidden-state geometry can be recovered from its behavior in psycholinguistic experiments. Across eight instruction-tuned transformer models, we run two experimental paradigms -- similarity-based forced choice and free association -- over a shared 5,000-word vocabulary, collecting 17.5M+ trials to build behavior-based similarity matrices. records.summary: Multi-agent systems promise a new axis for scaling inference: rather than having one agent think longer or sample more attempts, a task is split across many agents that work in parallel and coordinate. records.title: Distilling Text LMs into Speech-to-Speech LMs by Matching Internal Text Predictions
records.summary: Text language models (LMs) acquire broad linguistic and factual capabilities through large-scale pretraining, while comparable capabilities remain difficult to learn from speech alone. Recent work has shown that knowledge distillation from pretrained text LMs offers a promising way to transfer their linguistic and factual capabilities to speech models. However, existing distillation approaches have largely focused on speech-input, text-output models. This idea has yet to be explored for {\it speech-to-speech} models, which operate on both speech input and speech output. records.title: Compositional RL: Evaluating and Training LLMs for Collaborative Reasoning
records.summary: Language models are often evaluated alone but increasingly deployed together, routed between, made to debate, ensembled, or collaboratively trained. For a model inside a system, what matters most is not how well it performs on its own, but how much the system gains from its presence. We call this a model's compositional strength and formalize it using the Shapley value of a cooperative game over coalitions of a model pool, and use a model's leave-one-out contribution to the full coalition as a tractable proxy, requiring n+1 rather than 2^n system evaluations. records.title: The belief-action gap in language model agents
records.summary: Language model (LM) agents can fail for different reasons, requiring different explanations and interventions. We study how state beliefs, action values, and action preferences interact as LM agents reason and commit to decisions in text-rendered grid worlds. We estimate task-relevant beliefs using report-based and representation-based probes, and action values using inverse reinforcement learning. records.title: Plans Fade Fast: Why Context Management Is Load-Bearing for LLM Agents
records.summary: Context managers summarize or evict old messages so agents can operate beyond a finite window. This creates a reliability problem: removing history that still shapes the model's computation may change later actions, while retaining everything defeats compression. We study plans because agents create them early and are expected to use them later, yet behavioral success alone cannot reveal whether later calls still depend on the plan exchange. records.title: From Topology to Retrieval: Decoding Embedding Spaces with Unified Signatures
records.summary: Studying the shape of text embedding spaces enhances our understanding of model behavior and how geometry affects downstream task performance. While a range of topological and geometric metrics have been explored, they are typically analyzed in isolation, and the connections between them remain largely unknown. In this paper, we present Unified Topological Signatures (UTS) for characterizing the structure of embedding spaces. records.title: The Dynamics of Delusion: Modeling Bidirectional False Belief Amplification in Human-Chatbot Dialogue
records.summary: There is growing concern that AI chatbots might fuel delusional beliefs in users. Some have suggested that humans and chatbots mutually reinforce false beliefs over time, but quantitative evidence is lacking. Using a unique dataset of chat logs from individuals who exhibited delusional thinking, we developed a latent state model that captures accumulating and decaying influences between humans and chatbots. records.summary: Understanding a narrative means knowing how every event relates in time to every other, yet large language models (LLMs) are mostly tested on isolated event pairs or coarse labels. records.title: Phonological Interference in Multilingual Speech Models
records.summary: Phoneme-level models transcribe or generate speech as a sequence of phonemes, the smallest sound units that distinguish words. These models enable fine-grained pronunciation control and understanding, yet often fail on input that does not match any single training language, such as speech alternating between two languages, known as code-switching, or low-resource languages absent from training. We identify a systematic failure mode behind this, phonological interference: models assume the input is in a single language and impose its phonology, overriding local phoneme-level decisions that conflict with the assumed language. records.title: ControBench: An Interaction-Aware Benchmark for Controversial Discourse Analysis on Social Networks
records.summary: Understanding how people argue across ideological divides online is important for studying political polarization, misinformation, and content moderation. Existing datasets capture only part of this problem: some preserve text but ignore interaction structure, some model structure without rich semantics, and others represent conversations without stable user-level ideological identity. We introduce ControBench, a benchmark for controversial discourse analysis that combines heterogeneous social interaction graphs with rich textual semantics. records.title: Penumbra: Sample-Efficient Adversarial Search for Regulatory Obligations
records.summary: Agents are entering finance, healthcare and law, sectors where a violation leaves no lexical signature and carries real penalties.
